newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan textile stocks respond to relief package.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan textile stocks respond to relief package.

text.p: Pakistan's depressed textile stocks are showing signs of reviving in response to a government relief package to spinners aimed at spurring exports, analysts said on Tuesday.
"Several textile stocks have already moved up after the package and there are good prospects of posting more gains," Ali Raza Mooney of Kausar Abbas Bhayani Securities Ltd, said in a research report.

Floor brokers see a slow but steady rise in the values of textile stocks, which comprise one-third of the total listed companies on the Karachi Stock Exchange, Mooney said. "Future prospects in the textile sector are good," he added.

In seven trading sessions since the government unveiled the package on November 23, Nishat Mills shares have risen 4.22 percent to 18.50, Gadoon Textile 19.73 percent to 45.50 and Saif Textile 8.06 percent to 16.75.

The relief package was announced after pest attacks prompted ginners to scale back their estimate for the 1996/97 (July-June) cotton crop to 9.2 million 375-lb bales from an official target of 10 million.
High prices and successive crop shortfalls have led to the closure of more than 100 of Pakistan's 457 textile mills, while most of the rest were close to bankruptcy, Mooney said.

To rescue the textile industry, which accounts for more than 60 percent of Pakistan's foreign exchange earnings, the government decided to allow duty-free import of raw cotton and streamline procedures for collecting customs duty rebates.
"We believe that the positive impact of this package would be more striking for companies with some better past performance and better financial health," analyst Asif Janmohammad said.
But he said the fate of the spinning industry and the Pakistani economy was still closely tied to the cotton crop.
"Neither the industry nor the country is in a position to take the shock of another bad cotton crop," he added.
